title: Regional latency mitigation — status page update & customer summary (us-west-2)
content:
Purpose:
This doc packages two customer-facing artifacts for the us-west-2 latency incident: (1) a concise status-page update suitable for immediate public posting, and (2) a short post-incident customer summary that can be emailed to affected accounts or pasted into account-specific support threads. Use the suggested language verbatim for technical accuracy; where a customer account needs bespoke details (SLA uptime, request ids), edit the bracketed fields.

High-level summary (one-sentence for status page):
Between 2026-11-22T10:12:00Z and 2026-11-22T13:47:00Z a subset of inference requests routed through the us-west-2 serving pool experienced increased latency (observed 2x–8x above baseline). We mitigated customer impact by shifting traffic to warm-standby hosts in the same region, then to cross-region fallbacks, and restored normal latency by 13:47 UTC. No data loss; model outputs preserved.

Status page (short entry for immediate posting):
Title: Partial regional latency affecting inference in us-west-2 — mitigated
Impact: Some requests to models hosted in us-west-2 experienced elevated latencies; throughput for affected routes was reduced for a portion of traffic.
Action taken: Traffic was routed to warm standby pools and cross-region failovers while engineers applied a configuration rollback to the autoscaler kernel.
Current status: Service restored to normal latency for all routes as of 2026-11-22T13:47:00Z. Monitoring shows stable latencies within expected SLOs.
Next update: A customer-facing summary will be published in the next 72 hours with root cause and corrective actions.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (longer form):
Subject: Summary — us-west-2 latency incident on 2026-11-22
Hello [CustomerName],
We want to share what happened during the elevated latency event that affected some inference requests in the us-west-2 region on 2026-11-22. We recognize the disruption this may have caused and are committed to transparency and fixes to prevent recurrence.

What happened
- Window: 2026-11-22 10:12 UTC – 2026-11-22 13:47 UTC.
- Impact: A portion of inference requests routed to the us-west-2 serving pool experienced higher than expected latencies (2x–8x increase) and increased tail latency. Some requests were delayed beyond customer SLOs; a very small subset of requests retried by clients may have seen repeated delays while failover occurred. There was no loss of request payloads or model outputs.

Technical summary (concise)
- Trigger: An autoscaler policy triggered a burst of instance spin-ups coincident with a patched kernel update being rolled to a subset of GPU hosts. The interaction caused a scheduling regression in the GPU driver path for specific kernel versions, leading to transient thread starvation and elevated inference latency when the new instances joined the pool.
- Mitigation steps applied: 1) We immediately disabled the autoscaler burst for the pool. 2) We routed traffic preferentially to warm standby hosts in the same region (minimizing cross-region impact). 3) For traffic still affected, we initiated controlled cross-region fallback to our us-east-1 pool for high-priority routes. 4) We rolled back the kernel configuration on the impacted hosts and gradually returned traffic once latencies normalized.

Root cause (headline)
A kernel-level scheduling regression triggered by a recent driver/config rollout interacted poorly with autoscaler burst behavior, causing new instances to occasionally experience heavy scheduling latency for GPU-bound inference tasks.

Customer impact and data integrity
- Scope: Affects requests routed to the us-west-2 serving pool between timestamps above.
- Data: No request bodies or model outputs were lost. Logs and request IDs are preserved for auditing and can be provided on request.
- Recommended customer actions: If you observed repeated client retries or saw increases in downstream timeouts, please send relevant request IDs to your CSM or support rep so we can correlate traces. If you prefer region-level isolation, consider enabling pinned routing to a specific region or configuring model fallback policies to prefer dedicated pools.

Corrective and preventative actions (short term and long term)
Short-term (already executed)
- Rollback of the kernel configuration on affected hosts.
- Autoscaler burst temporarily disabled for the pool until safe rollout procedure is formalized.
- Traffic routing policy tightened to prefer healthy warm-standby hosts before cross-region fallback.
Long-term (in progress/planned)
- Harden rollout playbook: enforced canaries for kernel/driver updates with synthetic load tests for each canary stage.
- Autoscaler safeguards: add delay/verification step before admitting new instances into the GPU serving pool under production load.
- Observability: add GPU scheduling latency metric to the standard SLI set and surface early alerts at 2x baseline.
- Documentation: update public guidance for customers on routing/fallback best practices and introduce an API flag for aggressive isolation of customer traffic during host-level rollouts.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-11-22 10:10 — Pre-roll activity: kernel/driver rollout for a maintenance batch begins (canary stage scheduled).
- 2026-11-22 10:12 — Autoscaler burst triggered by a traffic spike; new instances started joining the us-west-2 pool.
- 2026-11-22 10:18 — Monitoring alerts: elevated p95/p99 GPU latency observed for the pool. Initial teams notified.
- 2026-11-22 10:30 — Engineers confirm correlation between new instances and spike; warm-standby routing enabled.
- 2026-11-22 11:05 — Cross-region fallback enabled for high-priority routes while investigation continues.
- 2026-11-22 12:20 — Decision to rollback kernel config on impacted hosts; rollback initiated.
- 2026-11-22 13:12 — Latencies trending down; gradual traffic reintroduction begins.
- 2026-11-22 13:47 — Metrics show restoration to SLOs. Incident declared mitigated.

How we will notify you
- Status page short entry (already posted) for immediate visibility.
- This customer summary will be sent to customers who experienced significant latency or who have open support threads.
- A formal, detailed postmortem with engineering timelines and RCA will be published within 72 hours to customers that request it or to enterprise accounts under NDA.

FAQ / Suggested CS responses (short bullets for triage agents)
Q: Was any user data lost?
A: No. Request payloads and model outputs are retained; no persisted customer data was corrupted or lost.

Q: Will I see any bill changes because of retries?
A: We are reviewing billing impact on a case-by-case basis. If your application performed automatic retries and you believe usage was materially higher as a result of this event, contact your account team and we will review credits where appropriate.

Q: What are the next steps I should take?
A: If you saw timeouts or exceptions, please share request IDs; consider enabling [model_fallback_policy] or pinning routes to a region until the enhanced rollout safeguards are in place.

Suggested plain-language email to customers (template)
Subject: Incident summary — us-west-2 inference latency (2026-11-22)
Hi [CustomerName],
We experienced elevated inference latencies for a subset of requests in us-west-2 on 2026-11-22. We mitigated the impact by routing traffic to standby hosts and rolling back a kernel configuration; service returned to normal at 13:47 UTC. No data was lost. We have short-term fixes in place and are implementing rollout and autoscaler safeguards to reduce the chance of recurrence.
If you have request IDs or traces from the window 10:12–13:47 UTC, please share them with your support contact so we can run a targeted analysis.
Thank you for your patience — we will follow up with a detailed engineering postmortem in the next 72 hours.
Best,
Maya Chen
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Notes-to-self for CS/Eng handoff (internal)
- Attach metrics dashboard links and a short list of impacted customers (filtered by routing logs) before sending the template email.
- Coordinate with billing to flag accounts with >5% anomalous increase in token usage between 10:12–13:47 UTC.
- Ensure PR #1789 (serving-runtime) includes the forced rollback and that the rollout pipeline is blocked for the next window until canaries and synthetic tests pass.

Open action items (owners):
- ENG: formal RCA and detailed postmortem (owner: Daniel Park) — due 2026-11-25.
- SRE: add GPU scheduling metric and alert (owner: Priya Kapoor) — due 2026-12-03.
- CS: send customer summary to impacted accounts after attaching per-account traces (owner: Maya Chen) — target 2026-11-23.

This doc is a living draft — please add suggested edits inline. For urgent updates, ping #incident-response-us-west on Slack.
